{"requested_url": "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sudofx/wake/85c611dfcb54e4918d7023e7cd07aec7f27dc14a/docs/architecture.md", "source_revision": "85c611dfcb54e4918d7023e7cd07aec7f27dc14a", "running_revision": "802c2de4a90f083fb7ab00a52091a64f1eb69d33", "source_search": "", "url": "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sudofx/wake/85c611dfcb54e4918d7023e7cd07aec7f27dc14a/docs/architecture.md", "scope": "raw source-controlled WAKE repository text", "excerpt": "# Architecture and limits

See [the reusable kernel contract](kernel.md) for application ownership and the
non-research execution proof, and [installation boundaries](installations.md) for
independent records and runtime lifecycles. These remain inside this repository.

The local [improvement application](improvements.md) uses that same kernel contract
in an explicitly new experiment record. Captured public research informs code
proposals; it does not become writable research authority. Untrusted candidate
code runs only in restricted disposable containers, while the host scores its
outputs. An operator review receipt cannot apply code or grant release authority.

The [autonomous context lane](autonomous-context.md) is a separate WAKE application
policy on the existing per-node native authority. An installed capability permits
one selector-field change, gated by recomputed fixed-task and current-native-state
measurements. Proposal generation, adoption and rollback require no per-change
human review. Metadata events preserve research versions and history; candidate
data cannot replace the evaluator, widen permissions, modify code or create a
competing research store. Native replay owns the policy after restart.

> **Current specification.** This document explains why the present system is shaped this way: its trust boundary, durable record, governance model and known limits. Current local procedures belong in `standalone.md`; public mirror publishing belongs in `cloud.md`. Maintainer navigation, environment checks and reproducible validation guidance belong in `development.md`.

**WAKE✳︎** is infrastructure for continuity of accountable work, not continuity of a model instance. Its stable sequence is **Record → Context → Proposal → Governance → Transition → Receipt**. {"url": "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=What+mechanisms+enable+an+intelligent+system+to+evaluate+whether+its+core+reward+function+or+objective+is+susceptible+to+adversarial+exploitation+or+misspecification%3F&format=json&resultType=core&pageSize=4", "scope": "Europe PMC search metadata, abstracts and full-text links; discovery only", "excerpt": "[{\"title\": \"SpiralEdge-IoV: secure and adaptive task offloading in internet of vehicles edge computing using logarithmic spiral defense.\", \"abstract\": \"In recent years, the internet of vehicles (IoV) has become an important enabler of intelligent transportation systems, providing vehicle-edge computing for latency-sensitive and computation-intensive vehicular applications. In such environments, the efficient offloading of tasks is pivotal; yet existing approaches primarily focus on optimising performance, often under the assumption of benign operating conditions or by employing static, trust-based mechanisms. However, these methods fall short in practical IoV implementations due to high mobility, short-lived connectivity, and the adversarial nature of IoV, where misbehaviour and resource exhaustion can substantially compromise the system's reliability and security. In response to these problems, we design SpiralEdge-IoV, a secure and adaptive task offloading framework that tightly integrates defence and optimisation. This framework embeds a logarithmic spiral defence (LSD) mechanism that models trust as a deepening, adaptive path over time, enabling online risk evaluation and incremental offensive action against suspicious parties. We integrate these risk scores into an in-built bio-inspired Addax-optimisation-based decision model (LSD-AddaxNet) to obtain security-aware multi-objective offloading decisions that not only minimise latency, energy consumption, and execution cost, but also maximise robustness. A combination of realistic vehicular edge-offloading traces and the VeReMi misbehaviour dataset is employed to conduct an extensive simulation-based evaluation, confirming the effectiveness of the proposed framework. Relative to representative optimisation- and learning-based baselines, SpiralEdge-IoV delivers up to 18% lower average task latency, reduces energy consumption by about 15%, and increases task success rates in adversarial settings by over 20%.
